learningObjectives: Distinguish steering an Excel workbook as a file from steering the Excel application's user interface.
Use the TBox Excel Standard Modules to open, manipulate, and close a workbook, respecting the mandatory open/close pattern.
Read, write, and verify cell contents and technical cell properties using Excel Ranges.
Compare two Excel workbooks and execute an existing Excel macro from a TestCase.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Two different ways to reach Excel

elements.description: Excel Standard Modules work with a workbook in the background without steering its visible window. Prefer data-level operations when the test concerns workbook data; inspect current engine prerequisites, including the executing user’s valid Office license.

The Excel UI Engine 3.0 scans and steers the Microsoft Excel user interface itself — the main application window, its dialogs, and the worksheets with embedded controls currently loaded by the application. Use it when the thing under test genuinely is the Excel UI: a dialog that must appear, a ribbon interaction, an embedded control a user would click.

elements.text: The choice matters for reliability. If you only need a cell's value, do not open Excel's window to read it — use the Standard Modules. Drive the UI only when the UI is the thing being tested.

elements.title: Excel Modules in the reviewed 2026.1 Standard subset
items: Open Excel Workbook — mandatory first step.
Close/Save Excel Workbook — required final step; controls saving.
Define Excel Range — declares the range later steps act on.
Manipulate Excel Range — read, write, and verify cell data and technical properties.
Clear Excel Range — clears content, formatting, notes, comments, hyperlinks or outlines.
Create Excel Worksheet — adds a sheet at a chosen position.
Delete Excel Worksheet — removes a sheet.
Update Excel Worksheet — renames and repositions a sheet.
Excel 1:1 File Compare — compares two workbooks.
Run Excel Macro — executes an existing macro.

bulletPoints: 'Steer an Excel workbook' → Standard Modules, background, file-level.
'Steer the Excel application' → Excel UI Engine 3.0, visible UI, control-level.

elements.description: The mandatory first step of any Excel Standard Module sequence. It opens the workbook in the background and can handle password-protected files and read-only access. Nothing else in the Excel Module family works until the workbook has been opened.

Close/Save Excel Workbook supports Save, Save & Close, or Close. Save Path controls the destination; Save As Type only applies with Save Path, and its type must match the file extension. Choose an operation that saves changes when required and closes resources at the end.

elements.text: Forgetting the Close step is the classic Excel automation mistake. The workbook stays open in the background, the file can remain locked, changes may not be written, and subsequent TestCases that touch the same file will fail for reasons that look unrelated.

bulletPoints: Every Excel Standard Module sequence is a sandwich: Open → (work) → Close.
Choose the Operation deliberately; a Close operation alone is not a request to save changes.

elements.description: Define a named range for manipulation. Choose Explicit start/end cells or Used Range; the selected range affects row/column counts and indexing.

The workhorse Module. It reads and writes cell data, and it also reaches the technical properties of cells — formulas, formatting, colors, fonts, and comments. Because it supports verification as well as input, this is the Module that satisfies the course objective 'verify Microsoft Excel cell special properties': you are not just checking the displayed value, you are checking that the underlying formula, the fill colour, or the font is what it should be.
Removes content from a range — and selectively, not just the values: formatting, notes, comments, hyperlinks, or outlines can each be cleared. Useful for resetting a sheet between test runs.

elements.text: Worksheet-level structure has its own Modules: Create Excel Worksheet (add a sheet, positioned first, last, or at a specific index), Delete Excel Worksheet, and Update Excel Worksheet (rename a sheet and move it within the workbook).
Technical cell properties include Formula and BackgroundColor. NumberFormat syntax can vary with the Office language setting; a correct displayed value does not prove the formula is correct.

bulletPoints: Define Range = declare where. Range Manipulation = read/write/verify what. Clear Range = reset.
'Cell special properties' means the technical layer — formula, formatting, colour, font, comment — not just the visible value.

elements.description: Excel 1:1 File Compare can check data, formatting and objects. Formatting and object comparisons are off by default; enable Include Formats and Include Objects when required. Select the relevant sheets and an Output Path for evidence.

Executes an existing Microsoft Excel macro from a TestStep, with a configurable timeout. Note the word existing — this Module runs a macro that already lives in the workbook; it is not a way to write VBA from Tosca. The timeout matters because a long-running macro would otherwise hang the TestCase.

elements.text: The original Academy Excel exercise files and exact lesson count were not obtained. These independent notes were compared with the 2026.1 public manual.

bulletPoints: Enable Include Formats and Include Objects explicitly when those checks are required.
Run Excel Macro triggers an existing macro; set the timeout deliberately.

examPitfalls.title: Omitting the Open or Close Excel Workbook step
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Dropping a Manipulate Excel Range Module straight into a TestCase and expecting it to work on its own.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: For workbook/range manipulation, open, define the range, manipulate and close/save as intended. File Compare uses file paths directly; do not impose this sequence on every Module indiscriminately.

examPitfalls.title: Driving the Excel UI when the file-level Modules would do
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Using the Excel UI Engine to open Excel's window and click through it just to read or write a cell value.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Prefer data-level Modules for data-only checks and UI Modules for supported interface behavior; validate reliability in the actual environment.

examPitfalls.title: Thinking 'cell special properties' means the displayed value
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Verifying only the text a cell shows and considering the cell fully tested.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Manipulate Excel Range also reaches technical properties — formulas, formatting, colours, fonts, comments. A cell can display the right number while holding the wrong formula, and only a property-level verification catches that.

examPitfalls.title: Expecting Run Excel Macro to create a macro
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Looking for a way to author VBA code inside the TestStep.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Run Excel Macro executes a macro that already exists in the workbook. Authoring the macro is outside Tosca's scope; Tosca triggers it and enforces a timeout.

examPitfalls.title: Saving on the wrong step
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Looking for a save option on the manipulation Modules after changing cell values.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Set Save or Save & Close when changes must be written. Check Save Path, file type and extension; Close alone is different.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A data-manipulation sequence must read and verify a workbook cell. Which Module opens the workbook before its range is defined?
practiceQuiz.hint: Nothing can be read from a workbook that has not been opened.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Open Excel Workbook establishes the workbook for this manipulation sequence; then define and manipulate the range. Close/Save releases it. File Compare is a separate path using Reference File and Target File paths; do not assume it needs the same open/range sequence.

optionExplanations.A: Define Range needs the opened workbook context.
optionExplanations.B: Open establishes the workbook for this manipulation sequence.
optionExplanations.C: Manipulate uses an already defined range.
optionExplanations.D: Running a macro is not opening the workbook.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A tester needs to confirm that a cell not only displays 1500 but also contains the correct SUM formula and the expected fill colour. Which Module handles this?
practiceQuiz.hint: The same Module that writes cell data also reaches the technical layer beneath it.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Manipulate Excel Range reads, writes and verifies both cell data and technical cell properties — formulas, formatting, colours, fonts and comments. This is what the objective 'verify Excel cell special properties' refers to.

optionExplanations.A: File Compare checks files rather than this individual cell-property requirement.
optionExplanations.B: Clear removes data or formatting rather than verifies it.
optionExplanations.C: Manipulate can verify Formula and BackgroundColor in the defined range.
optionExplanations.D: Create Worksheet changes structure, not these cell properties.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Where do you configure whether an edited workbook is saved, and to which path and file format?

options.text: On each Manipulate Excel Range step

practiceQuiz.hint: The decision about what happens to the file belongs to the step that finishes with it.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Close/Save Excel Workbook controls its Operation and save destination. Save As Type requires Save Path and a matching extension; changing data does not itself guarantee the requested file is saved.

optionExplanations.A: Open sets loading, not this save destination.
optionExplanations.B: Manipulation changes contents, not the save operation.
optionExplanations.C: Close/Save selects the save operation and destination/type.
optionExplanations.D: These settings belong to the Module, not a universal project default.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A generated Excel report must match an expected reference file, including formatting and embedded objects — not just cell values. Which Module fits?

options.text: Two Manipulate Excel Range steps compared manually

practiceQuiz.hint: There is a dedicated comparison Module, and it goes beyond cell contents.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Excel 1:1 File Compare fits this requirement, with Include Formats and Include Objects enabled. They are not enabled by default. Define Range and Update Worksheet do not perform this file comparison.

optionExplanations.A: File Compare supports the required checks when the relevant options are enabled.
optionExplanations.B: Define Range establishes cells for manipulation, not a file comparison.
optionExplanations.C: Update Worksheet renames or reorders a sheet.
optionExplanations.D: Manual checks do not replace the dedicated file-comparison result.

practiceQuiz.scenario: When should you use the Excel UI Engine 3.0 rather than the Excel Standard Modules?

options.text: Always — it is the more modern approach.
When the Excel user interface itself is what is being tested: application window, dialogs, or embedded controls a user would interact with.
Only when the workbook is password protected.
Whenever a cell value needs to be read.

practiceQuiz.hint: One approach drives a visible UI; the other works on the file in the background.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Use Excel UI Engine for visible dialogs, worksheets and supported embedded controls. For a data-only requirement, Standard Modules avoid unnecessary UI steering; this is a test-design choice, not a universal performance guarantee.

optionExplanations.A: Choose based on the tested behavior, not a universal preference.
optionExplanations.B: UI steering fits these visible-interface requirements.
optionExplanations.C: Background opening also supports password-protected workbooks.
optionExplanations.D: Data-level Modules can read values without testing the UI.

quickRecap.value: Standard Modules = file-level, background. Excel UI Engine 3.0 = the visible Excel application.
Manipulation: Open → Define Range → work → Close/Save. File Compare takes reference and target paths directly.
Close/Save Operation chooses Save, Save & Close or Close; Save As Type requires Save Path and matching extension.
Define Excel Range (where) → Excel Range Manipulation (read/write/verify, incl. formulas, formatting, colours, fonts, comments) → Clear Excel Range (reset).
Create / Delete / Update Excel Worksheet — add, remove, rename and reposition sheets.
File Compare: cell data by default; enable formats/objects explicitly; optional text output.
Run Excel Macro — executes an EXISTING macro, with a configurable timeout.
